summary: Every new worktree used to start with no node_modules, so the agent ran npm install and the machine ended up with one full copy per worktree - measured at ~700MB each on the user's Mac across 6 worktrees, with the disk at 94% full. cloneDependencyDirs(sourceRoot, worktreeRoot) now fires in the background, right after a worktree is confirmed to exist on disk, and requests a copy-on-write clone of the source project's root node_modules into the new worktree: `cp -c -R` (APFS clonefile) on macOS, `cp -R --reflink=always` on Linux (btrfs/XFS only - it fails outright on ext4, which is intentional). Before invoking `cp` at all, it verifies the source and the worktree are on the same device (fs.stat().dev, rules out crossing volumes on either platform) and, on macOS specifically, that the destination's filesystem is actually APFS (shelling out to `mount` and reading the type it prints, since Node exposes no documented filesystem-type string and `fs.statfs().type` is an unstable magic number) - required because `cp -c` does not error when clonefile is unavailable, it silently performs a real full copy instead (verified on this Mac: `cp -c -R` across an HFS+ volume exits 0 and produces a byte-for-byte copy with no sharing), so the exit code can never be trusted to catch that case. Any unsupported platform, cross-device pair, non-APFS macOS target, or command failure does nothing and logs once; there is deliberately no full-copy fallback, because that would silently make the disk-space problem worse. The clone writes into a staging directory beside the real target (node_modules.sb-clone-<random>, same worktree, so the final step is an atomic same-volume rename) rather than straight into <worktree>/node_modules, because the worktree is already usable the moment git worktree add returns and an agent's own npm install could start racing this background clone; the staged clone is discarded (and the destination left completely untouched) if node_modules exists by the time the clone finishes, and a failed clone or failed rename only ever removes the staging directory. The clone never blocks or fails worktree creation: it is fire-and-forget, wrapped so it can never throw into its caller. Wired into every place that runs `git worktree add` for a project: the three flows in src/main/worktree.ts (kanban card, fork-from-message, session - kept for back-compat/tests even though production traffic has moved off them), plus the two call sites that actually run in production today, ExecFileGitWorktreeAdapter.materialize (kanban card creation and fork-to-worktree, via the atomic WorktreeCreationService) and GitLegacySessionWorktreeMaterializer.materialize (new-session-in-worktree-mode, despite the 'legacy' file name). Opt-out via the existing generic settings table: worktree.cloneDependencies = 'false' disables it; unset or any other value means on. The setting is read only once there is actually something to clone (source has node_modules, destination doesn't), so the common no-op case never touches the settings DB.

reactNativeIos.reason: The mobile app is a thin client over WsTransport/IapTransport to a backend host; it never runs git, npm, or a filesystem clone locally and has no node_modules of its own. Worktree creation, and now the dependency clone that follows it, happens entirely on whichever backend (desktop Electron main process or the standalone headless server) the phone is paired with. This change is invisible on the wire - no new IPC channel, no new event - so there is nothing for the mobile client to implement.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same reasoning as reactNativeIos: native Android is a thin client with no local git/npm/filesystem-clone concept and no visibility into backend-side worktree materialization.

updateRelease.reason: No wire protocol, package identity, native module, version, or packaging change. This is a background filesystem helper spawned via execFile (no new dependency) inside existing main-process code; nothing here touches update channels or release packaging.

automated: npx vitest run tests/unit/dependency-clone.test.ts (18 tests): per-platform command/argv against a staging path (darwin cp -c -R, linux cp -R --reflink=always) followed by an atomic rename into node_modules, unsupported-platform no-op, source-missing skip with no log (ENOENT is the expected no-op case) and confirms the settings DB is never touched in that common case, a non-ENOENT error checking the source is logged and skipped, destination-exists skip, opt-out setting disabled, a cross-device source/worktree pair skips without calling cp and without running the (more expensive) APFS check, a macOS destination not confirmed APFS skips without calling cp, the APFS check does not run at all on linux, a failed clone removes only its staging dir and leaves no node_modules, a node_modules that appears mid-clone (simulating a concurrent npm install) is left completely untouched and the losing staged clone is discarded, the function never rejects even when the runner throws, the fire-and-forget wrapper never throws synchronously, isDependencyCloneEnabled's default-on / literal-'false'-only-disables semantics, and one unmocked end-to-end run on this machine (darwin) exercising the real same-device and real `mount`-based APFS checks together, not just injected fakes.

npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree.test.ts tests/unit/create-session-worktree.test.ts: existing worktree-creation tests still pass unchanged with the background clone call wired in (fire-and-forget, so it does not interfere with the existing GitRunner stubs).

npx vitest run tests/unit/worktree-creation-git-adapter.test.ts tests/unit/legacy-session-worktree-lease.test.ts tests/unit/fork-worktree-request.test.ts tests/unit/git-legacy-worktree-handler.test.ts: the real ExecFileGitWorktreeAdapter and GitLegacySessionWorktreeMaterializer, exercised against real git in temp fixture repos with no node_modules, still pass - confirming the added call is a true no-op when there is nothing to clone.
hardware: Measured on the user's Mac (real APFS filesystem, no mocks): confirmed the exact failure mode this change guards against - `cp -c -R` from a directory into a scratch HFS+-formatted disk image (created with `hdiutil create -fs HFS+`) exits 0 and produces a byte-for-byte real copy, with no clonefile sharing, proving the exit code alone cannot detect a silent full-copy fallback. Then ran the real cloneDependencyDirs(sourceRoot, worktreeRoot) - real same-device check, real `mount`-based APFS check, no mocks - against this repo's own live node_modules (934MB by `du -sh`) as the source and a fresh mkdtemp destination via `npx vite-node -c vitest.config.ts`, across two runs: 6.3s and 9.4s wall clock. `df -k /` showed the same `Used` figure before and after both runs, with only ordinary background `Available` drift, despite the destination reporting the full 934-944MB under `du -sh` and only a single `node_modules` directory left behind (the staging directory was gone, confirming the atomic rename ran) - confirming the clone is block-shared (copy-on-write), not a real copy. The scratch HFS+ disk image, the scratch destination directories, and the throwaway settings DB dir were all removed after the measurements.
notExercised: The Linux (`--reflink=always`) path itself was exercised only by unit tests with a mocked runner - no real btrfs/XFS filesystem was available to confirm the actual clonefile/reflink behavior or its ext4 hard-failure, on this Mac. The same-device check ahead of it is platform-agnostic and IS covered by the real, unmocked integration test.

The `mount`-output parsing that backs the macOS APFS check was verified against exactly two real filesystem types on this Mac (apfs, hfs) and against `mount`'s current output format on this macOS version - it has not been checked against every fstype string macOS can report (msdos, exfat, smbfs, nfs, autofs, ...), nor against a `mount` output format change in a future macOS release. Any of those either match 'apfs' (extremely unlikely) or fail the match and correctly skip the clone, so the failure mode of an unrecognized format is a missed clone, not a wrong one.
The headless server (src/server, WsHost) was not run end-to-end on a remote Linux VM for this change; the shared code path is exercised by unit tests only, not a live remote worktree creation.

The three creation flows in src/main/worktree.ts (createWorktree, createForkWorktree, createSessionWorktree) are not reachable from any current production IPC handler - production kanban/fork/session worktree creation now goes through ExecFileGitWorktreeAdapter and GitLegacySessionWorktreeMaterializer instead. The clone call was added to all three anyway per the task's explicit instruction and for back-compat if a caller returns, but it has no live traffic today.

The concurrent-npm-install race (staged clone discarded when node_modules appears mid-clone) is covered by a unit test that simulates the race inside the fake runner, not by an actual concurrent `npm install` process running against a real clone.
